data.prompt: Run your `has_pair` function on a list that contains exactly one element, e.g., `a=[3]`, with `target=6`. Observe the returned value and note which part of the algorithm allowed the same index to be used for both `lo` and `hi`.

data.expected_insight: The loop condition `while lo <= hi` lets `lo` equal `hi`, so the algorithm can add the same element to itself. Changing the guard to `while lo < hi` (or otherwise ensuring distinct indices) prevents this boundary case from producing a false positive.
